protocol.name: cupertino_app_effects_v1

description.summary: effects any client may ask the server to draw for its own windows

protocol.description: Public protocol: the material backdrops and the title bar style of a client's own surfaces, the appearance of the session and the address of the menus its windows export. A request names surfaces of the client that sends it; the server never lets a client change the look of another client's surface. Nothing here gives control over other clients, the windows' arrangement or the session; those roles are in the private cupertino_shell_v1.

interface.name: cupertino_app_effects_v1

description.summary: effects for the client's own surfaces

interface.description: Global singleton, offered to every client. Version 2 adds get_menu, version 3 the menu_reader event of cupertino_app_menu_v1, version 4 set_disabled_controls; the other interfaces of the protocol are unchanged in each.

entry.name: invalid_surface
entry.summary: the surface belongs to another client or is gone

entry.name: window
entry.summary: the surface is not an application window, or the window is already mapped

entry.name: too_many_backdrops
entry.summary: the surface or the client holds as many backdrops as the server allows

entry.name: menu_exists
entry.summary: the surface already has a menu announcement

entry.name: invalid_controls
entry.summary: a bit not defined at the object's version

enum.name: titlebar_style

description.summary: how the server decorates an application window

enum.description: Applies to windows the server decorates (xdg-decoration server-side mode).

entry.name: standard
entry.summary: a title bar above the surface, drawn by the server with the window's title

entry.name: unified
entry.summary: the surface fills the whole window and the title bar lies over its top; the server draws only the window control buttons

enum.name: window_control

description.summary: the window controls a client may disable

enum.description: The close button is not among them: a window can always be closed.

entry.name: minimize
entry.summary: the minimize button, the minimize shortcut and the Window menu's Minimize

entry.name: zoom
entry.summary: the zoom button, the zoom shortcut, the Window menu's Zoom, the title bar's double click and the fill tile

request.name: destroy

description.summary: unbind the global

request.description: Objects created through this global stay valid.

request.name: get_backdrop

description.summary: create a material backdrop under a surface

request.description: Creates a backdrop drawn by the server directly below the surface's content: the pixels behind the region are blurred and coloured by a material recipe and composited through a rounded mask. The client draws only its own content, usually with a transparent background. A surface may have several backdrops; they are drawn in creation order, all below the surface. A new backdrop has no material and draws nothing until the material and shape are set and the surface is committed. Posts invalid_surface when the surface belongs to another client, and too_many_backdrops when the surface already has 64 backdrops or the client has 128 (the limits count the backdrops that are not destroyed yet).

request.name: set_titlebar_style

description.summary: choose the title bar style of an application window

request.description: Chooses how the server decorates the xdg toplevel of the surface. The default is standard. With the unified style the surface starts at the top edge of the window: the client draws its toolbar, the fill behind it and the window's title in the top strip, and keeps the area of the window control buttons at the strip's leading edge free of controls, because the buttons take the pointer there. The server does not move the window from the strip: the client does, with xdg_toplevel.move, and a double click may call xdg_toplevel.set_maximized. Resize zones and the window shape are the server's in both styles. Posts invalid_surface when the surface belongs to another client, and window when it is not an xdg toplevel or has committed a buffer.

request.name: get_appearance

description.summary: follow the appearance of the session

request.description: Creates an observer of the appearance and the accessibility display options. It has no surface, so a client may create any number of them. The server sends the current state right after the object is created and again on every change.

request.name: get_menu

description.summary: announce the menus of an application window

request.description: Creates the object through which the client announces where the menus of the window of the surface are exported on the session bus, and learns whether the desktop's menu bar shows them. Posts invalid_surface when the surface belongs to another client, and menu_exists when the surface already has a cupertino_app_menu_v1 that is not destroyed.

request.name: set_disabled_controls

description.summary: disable window controls of an application window

request.description: Disables the controls of the xdg toplevel of the surface. A disabled button is drawn dimmed and takes no click, and the matching shortcut and Window menu items do nothing on this window, nor, for zoom, does a double click on the title bar or filling the screen by tiling (half and quarter tiles stay possible). The client's own xdg_toplevel.set_minimized and xdg_toplevel.set_maximized are refused too. Unzooming a window that is already zoomed and restoring a minimized one stay possible, so a window is never kept zoomed or minimized by this request. The state is double-buffered: it applies at the surface's next wl_surface.commit. It may change at any time, also after the window is mapped. The default is none. The close button can't be disabled. Hide, the application switcher, the overview, the moves between workspaces and Force Quit act on the window as on any other, and full screen is not a window control: the client asks for it itself. A window that isn't resizable (its minimum size equals its maximum size) has zoom disabled whatever this says. Posts invalid_surface when the surface belongs to another client, window when it is not an xdg toplevel, and invalid_controls when disabled has a bit the object's version does not define.

interface.name: cupertino_backdrop_v1

description.summary: a material region below a surface

interface.description: All state is double-buffered: it applies on the next wl_surface.commit of the surface the backdrop was created for, together with that commit's buffer, so the backdrop and the content always move together. When the surface is destroyed the backdrop becomes inert.

entry.name: unknown_material
entry.summary: the material name is not a recipe of the server's design tokens

entry.name: invalid_shape
entry.summary: negative width or height, or a negative corner radius

request.name: destroy

description.summary: remove the backdrop

request.description: The backdrop disappears with the next commit of its surface.

request.name: set_material

description.summary: choose the material recipe

request.description: Name of a material recipe of the design tokens, for example "Menu" or "Sidebar". The server picks the light or dark variant from the current appearance.

request.name: set_shape

description.summary: set the region and its corner radius

request.description: Rectangle in surface-local logical coordinates and the radius of its continuous corners in logical points. A zero width or height hides the backdrop.

request.name: set_alpha

description.summary: set the opacity of the whole backdrop

request.description: Opacity from 0 to 1 applied to the composited backdrop, for fades. The initial value is 1.

interface.name: cupertino_appearance_v1

description.summary: appearance and display options of the session

interface.description: Right after the object is created the server sends appearance, then display_options. Later events say what changed; an event is complete by itself and is not part of a group.

description.summary: stop observing the appearance

event.name: appearance

description.summary: the session's appearance

event.description: 1 for the dark appearance, 0 for the light one. The client draws again with it, for example from the colours of its materials and palettes. The materials of the client's backdrops follow the appearance in the server and need no request.

entry.name: differentiate_without_color
entry.summary: do not carry state by colour alone

event.name: display_options

description.summary: the accessibility display options of the session

event.description: The options that are on. The client draws again with them: with reduce_motion it fades what it would slide, scale or magnify; with reduce_transparency and increase_contrast it picks its opaque and high-contrast palettes. The materials of the client's backdrops follow the options in the server and need no request. Bits the client does not know are reserved and stay 0.

interface.name: cupertino_app_menu_v1

description.summary: the menus of an application window

interface.description: The window's menus are exported on the session bus as org.gtk.Menus objects and their actions as org.gtk.Actions objects. The server hands the address to the desktop's menu bar while the window is active; it reads nothing on the bus itself. Right after the object is created the server sends menu_bar, and from version 3 menu_reader, and each again whenever its value changes.

entry.name: invalid_address
entry.summary: a bus name or object path is malformed or too long

request.name: destroy

description.summary: withdraw the announcement

request.description: The menu bar stops showing the window's exported menus.

request.name: set_address

description.summary: where the window's menus are exported

request.description: bus_name is the unique name (":1.42") of the client's connection that serves the objects. application_object_path serves the app actions, window_object_path the win actions, menubar_object_path the window's menus, and app_menu_object_path the application menu, or is empty when the client exports none. A later request replaces the address. Posts invalid_address when bus_name is not a unique bus name, a path is not an object path, or a path is longer than 512 bytes.

event.name: menu_bar

description.summary: whether the desktop's menu bar shows the window's menus

event.description: 1 while a menu bar runs and shows the menus the client announces; the client then draws no menu bar inside the window. 0 while none runs; the client shows its menus itself. From version 3 it is 1 only while menu_reader names a connection too: a menu bar that cannot read the menus does not stand in for them. menu_reader comes before menu_bar 1, and menu_bar 0 before menu_reader is emptied.

event.name: menu_reader

description.summary: the only bus connection that may use the window's menus

event.description: The unique name (":1.42") of the menu bar's bus connection, after the server checked that the connection belongs to the menu bar process; empty while there is none. The client answers no other peer: not its org.gtk.Menus reads, not its org.gtk.Actions calls, and sends its Changed signals to this connection alone.
